docs.title: SwingPy
docs.text: SwingPy is a Python library for the simulation of pressure, vacuum and vacuum-pressure swing adsorption cycles (PSA, VSA, VPSA). It solves a one-dimensional, nonisothermal and nonisobaric column model with any number of gas components, and runs cycles built from simple steps to cyclic steady state, with their purity, recovery, energy and productivity.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
• Column model: axially dispersed plug flow, linear driving force uptake, bed and wall energy balances, Darcy or Ergun pressure drop; finite volumes with WENO or flux-limited schemes, solved by a stiff integrator with a sparse Jacobian (optionally compiled with numba).
  • Equilibrium: competitive dual-site Langmuir, Sips and Toth isotherms, on a concentration or partial pressure basis.
  • Cycles: every step is two boundary conditions, one per column end: feed, pressurization, blowdown, evacuation with vacuum pumps, purge, light product pressurization, light and heavy reflux, pressure equalization. Steps can end on a pressure. Recorded streams couple steps in one column to stand for a multi-bed plant.
  • Results: purity, recovery, energy and productivity from exact running integrals, mass and energy balance errors, cyclic steady state on both the mass balance and the column profiles, and a full set of figures.
  • Data: a bank of adsorbents and gases, extensible with your own files.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
• Installation

First public release: finite volume model of pressure, vacuum and vacuum-pressure swing adsorption columns (PSA, VSA, VPSA), cycles to cyclic steady state with coupled steps and vector acceleration, a data bank of gases, problem specifications (swingpy.spec, with example input files and setups in examples), Langmuir, Sips, Toth, extended Langmuir and IAST isotherms, particle diffusion, a family of single-column VSA cycles (swingpy.cycles.vsa_cycle) with presets for the seven cycle configurations of Haghpanah et al. (2013), and a complete set of tables and figures of every simulation.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
SwingPy needs Python 3.10 or later, NumPy and SciPy.

pip install "swingpy @ git+https://github.com/mohammmadyazdani/swingpy.git"

Optional features are installed as extras:

Extra Adds Use fast numba compiled right-hand side, several times faster cycles plot matplotlib figures test pytest the test suite 
pip install "swingpy[fast,plot] @ git+https://github.com/mohammmadyazdani/swingpy.git"

From a clone of the repository, for development:

pip install -e ".[fast,plot,test,docs]"
pytest
mkdocs serve        # this documentation, locally

docs.title: A breakthrough
docs.text:
from swingpy import (Adsorbent, Column, ColumnModel, DualSiteLangmuir, FeedInlet, MacroporeLDF, PressureOutlet,
                      Step, data)

gas = data.gas(["CO2", "N2"], {"CO2": 0.15, "N2": 0.85})
sorbent = Adsorbent(
    name="zeolite 13X",
    isotherm=DualSiteLangmuir(qsb=(3.09, 5.84), qsd=(2.54, 0.0), b0=(8.65e-7, 2.5e-6), d0=(2.63e-8, 0.0),
                              dUb=(-36641.0, -15800.0), dUd=(-35691.0, 0.0)),
    heat_of_adsorption=(36641.0, 15800.0), density=1130.0, particle_radius=1e-3, particle_voidage=0.35,
    tortuosity=3.0, heat_capacity=1070.0, adsorbed_phase_heat_capacity=30.7, kinetics=MacroporeLDF())
column = Column(length=1.0, inner_radius=0.1445, bed_voidage=0.37)
model = ColumnModel(column, sorbent, gas, n_cells=30)

feed = Step("FEED", 3000.0,
            feed_end=FeedInlet(1.0, {"CO2": 0.15, "N2": 0.85}),
            product_end=PressureOutlet(1.0))
result = model.simulate(feed, model.initial_state(1.0, {"N2": 1.0}), n_output=301)
exit_gas = model.end_history(result, "product")     # velocity, pressure, temperature, composition

docs.title: A four-step VSA cycle
docs.text:
from swingpy import Cycle, ExponentialRamp, PressurizationInlet
from swingpy.plotting import plot_all

high, intermediate, low = 1.0, 0.1, 0.03
cycle = Cycle([
    Step("PRES", 15.0,
         feed_end=PressurizationInlet(ExponentialRamp(low, high, 0.5), {"CO2": 0.15, "N2": 0.85})),
    Step("FEED", 80.0, feed_end=FeedInlet(1.0, {"CO2": 0.15, "N2": 0.85}),
         product_end=PressureOutlet(high, stream="raffinate")),
    Step("BLOW", 30.0, product_end=PressureOutlet(ExponentialRamp(high, intermediate, 0.5),
                                                      stream="waste")),
    Step("EVAC", 40.0, feed_end=PressureOutlet(ExponentialRamp(intermediate, low, 0.5),
                                                     stream="product")),
], key_component="CO2")

run = cycle.run(model, model.initial_state(low, {"N2": 1.0}))
print(run.performance.purity, run.performance.recovery, run.performance.specific_energy)
plot_all(model, run.recent, run.history, "Four step VSA")      # every figure of the run

run.performance holds the purity, recovery, specific energy and productivity of the last cycle, run.history those of every cycle, and run.recent the full results of the last ten cycles.

docs.title: swingpy.boundaries
docs.text:
Boundary conditions at the two ends of the column.

A cycle step is defined by what happens at the feed end (Z = 0) and at the product end (Z = 1). Each end is described by one of the classes below, so a new step is built by combining two of them rather than by editing the model. The same class works at either end: for example PressureOutlet at the product end is a blowdown, and at the feed end it is an evacuation.

User inputs are in practical units: pressures in bar, velocities in m/s (interstitial), temperatures in K, compositions as dicts or sequences of mole fractions. The model converts them internally.

Every boundary also says what kind of stream it is (stream), which the cycle uses to compute purity and recovery, and which machine moves the gas (a compressor fed from supply_pressure, or a vacuum pump discharging to discharge_pressure), which the cycle uses to compute energy.

docs.title: Efficiency = Union[float, Callable[[float], float]] module-attribute
docs.text: A machine efficiency: a number, or a function of the suction pressure in bar.

docs.title: STANDARD_MOLAR_VOLUME = 0.022414 module-attribute
docs.text: Molar volume of an ideal gas at 0 C and 1 atm, m3/mol, for flows given in standard litres.

docs.title: Constant
docs.text: A pressure that does not change during the step, in bar.

docs.title: ExponentialRamp dataclass
docs.text:
Pressure relaxing exponentially from start to end (bar):

P(t) = end + (start - end) exp(-rate t)

a common way of prescribing the pressure history of pressurization, blowdown and evacuation steps, with rate the constant lambda in 1/s.

docs.title: LinearRamp dataclass
docs.text:
Pressure changing linearly from start to end (bar) over duration (s), then held at end:

P(t) = start + (end - start) min(t / duration, 1)

as used for the feed pressurization of Nguyen et al. (Chem. Eng. J. 452 (2023) 139550, Eq. 9).

docs.title: PressureOutlet
docs.text:
Bases: Boundary

Gas leaving while the face pressure is held or ramped: a back pressure regulator (constant pressure) or a vacuum pump following a prescribed pressure history (blowdown and evacuation).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default pressure

Face pressure in bar, a number or a history.

required discharge_pressure

Pressure the gas is delivered to, bar. Energy is charged for pumping from the face pressure up to it.

1.0 efficiency Efficiency

Vacuum pump efficiency, a number or a function of the suction pressure such as falling_vacuum_efficiency.

Stream label, "waste" by default; use "product" for the stream whose purity and recovery are reported.

'waste' record_as

Name under which the outgoing stream is recorded, so that a later step can use it (BufferInlet, TankInlet).

None check_valve

Let gas only leave: while the column is below the set pressure the face stays closed (for example while the feed brings a column back up from sub-atmospheric pressure).

False

docs.title: BufferInlet
docs.text:
Bases: Boundary

Gas entering from a recorded stream, replayed in time: the molar flow, composition and temperature follow the record of another step. Used for light product pressurization and light reflux, where the raffinate of the adsorption step enters the column at the product end.

The molar flow is imposed, so the velocity follows from v P / T at the face (equivalently v = v_source P_source / P). When the record is exhausted or not yet available (first cycle), no gas enters.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default buffer

Name of the record (record_as of the source outlet).

required offset

Time into the record at which the replay starts, s. Lets two steps share one record, for example light reflux using the first t_LR seconds of the raffinate and pressurization the rest.

0.0 stream

Stream label of the recycled gas.

'raffinate' max_pressure

Pressure of the source, bar. Gas cannot enter a column at a higher pressure than the one it is supplied at, so when the recorded flow would need a higher face pressure, the face is held at max_pressure and the flow follows from the pressure drop instead (it falls to zero as the column approaches that pressure). Without it the recorded flow is imposed whatever the pressure, which over-pressurizes the column near the end of a light product pressurization.

None composition

Replay only the recorded molar flow, with this gas instead of the recorded one (mole fractions, dict or sequence), for example a single column simulation of pressure equalization with pure product gas. None (default) replays the recorded composition.

None

docs.title: TankInlet
docs.text:
Bases: Boundary

Gas entering at a constant molar flow from a well mixed tank, used for heavy reflux: a fraction of the extract of a recorded step is sent back to the feed end over the duration of this step. The composition is the mean composition of the recorded stream.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default buffer

Name of the record that fills the tank.

required fraction

Fraction of the recorded moles fed back (reflux ratio).

required temperature

Temperature of the gas leaving the tank, K.

298.15 supply_pressure

Tank pressure, bar; a compressor is charged above it.

1.0 efficiency Efficiency

Compressor efficiency.

0.72 stream

Stream label, "product" by default, so that the refluxed gas is subtracted from the product.

'product'

docs.title: VacuumPump
docs.text:
Bases: Boundary

A vacuum pump of constant volumetric flow drawing gas out of the column.

The pump fixes the actual volumetric flow at the column end, and hence the interstitial velocity v = S / (eps A), while the face pressure follows from the pressure drop over half a cell. How long it takes to reach a given vacuum is then a result of the simulation rather than an input, so the step is usually ended with stop=PressureReached(...). This gives more realistic step times and pump sizes than prescribed pressure histories.

The pump is given either by its capacity or by the interstitial velocity it draws. The velocity keeps its meaning when an optimizer changes the column diameter; the capacity is then computed from it.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default volumetric_flow

Pump capacity at suction conditions, m3/h.

None velocity

Interstitial velocity at the column end, m/s (instead of volumetric_flow).

None discharge_pressure

Pressure the gas is delivered to, bar.

1.01325 efficiency Efficiency

Pump efficiency, a number or a function of the suction pressure such as falling_vacuum_efficiency.

0.72 stream

Stream label.

'waste' record_as

Name under which the pumped stream is recorded.

None

docs.text:

Gas entering at a fixed molar flow, as set by a mass flow controller.

The velocity follows from the flow and the face pressure; composition and temperature from the Danckwerts conditions. With max_pressure the face cannot rise above the supply pressure: once the flow would need a higher face pressure, the face is held there and the flow follows from the pressure drop (a pressurization that stops at the supply pressure).

Parameters:

mol/s (use standard_litres_per_minute for flows in L/min STP).

required composition

Mole fractions of the entering gas, or the name of a recorded stream whose mean composition enters.

required default_composition

Composition used while that record does not exist yet.

None temperature

K.

298.15 max_pressure

Supply pressure, bar, or None for no limit.

None supply_pressure

Pressure of the supply, bar; a compressor is charged above it.

None efficiency Efficiency

Efficiency of that compressor.

0.72 stream

Stream label.

'feed'

docs.title: MixingInlet
docs.text:
Bases: Boundary

Fresh gas at a fixed molar flow mixed with gas recycled from a well mixed tank, for a recycle into the feed: the outlet of an earlier step is collected (record_as) and sent back, spread evenly over this step, together with the fresh feed.

The recycled gas enters at temperature like the fresh gas (it is cooled to the feed temperature). The fresh moles count as the stream stream and the recycled ones as recycle_stream, so that recovery is computed on the fresh feed only and the recycle nets out against the step it came from (label that outlet with the same recycle_stream).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default molar_flow

Fresh gas, mol/s.

required composition

Mole fractions of the fresh gas.

required buffer

Name of the record that fills the tank.

required fraction

Fraction of the recorded moles sent back.

1.0 temperature

Temperature of the mixture, K.

298.15 supply_pressure

Pressure of the supply, bar; a compressor is charged above it.

None efficiency Efficiency

Efficiency of that compressor.

0.72 stream

Label of the fresh gas ("feed").

'feed' recycle_stream

Label of the recycled gas ("recycle").

'recycle'

docs.title: RecordedPressure
docs.text:
A reservoir pressure taken from the face pressure that another step recorded (record_as), typically in the previous cycle.

In a multi-bed plant a bed that equalizes or supplies purge vents into another bed, whose pressure changes during the step. A single-column simulation records the face pressure of the receiving step and uses it as the downstream pressure of the donor step one cycle later; at cyclic steady state the two are consistent.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default buffer

Name of the record.

required default

Pressure in bar before any record exists (first cycle), a number or a function of time in s.

required

Valve coefficient, mol/(s bar).

docs.title: swingpy.steps
docs.text:
Cycle steps.

A step is the pair of boundary conditions at the two column ends and a duration, with an optional condition that ends it early.

docs.title: Step dataclass
docs.text:
One step of a cycle.

Attributes:

Name Type Description name str

Display name, for example "adsorption".

Step time, s.

Boundary condition at Z = 0.

docs.title: swingpy.cycle
docs.text:
Cycles, cyclic steady state and key performance indicators.

A cycle is a list of steps run one after the other on a single column; the state at the end of a step is the initial state of the next one. The key performance indicators are computed from the stream labels of the boundary conditions, so they work for any cycle: the purity and recovery of the key_component are taken in the stream labelled product against the streams labelled feed.

docs.title: CyclePerformance dataclass
docs.text:
Key performance indicators of one cycle.

Attributes:

Name Type Description purity float

Mole fraction of the key component in the product stream, %.

recovery float

Key component in the product over key component fed, %.

mass_balance_error float

|in - out| / in of the key component over the cycle, %.

specific_energy float

Machine work per tonne of key component in the product, kWh/t.

productivity float

Key component in the product per adsorbent volume and cycle time, mol/(m3 s). The adsorbent volume is (1 - eps) A L.

cycle_time float

Sum of the actual step durations, s (steps with a stop condition may end early or be skipped).

energy_by_step dict

Machine work of each step, J.

streams dict

Net moles of each component in each labelled stream per cycle, positive out of the column.

heat_by_step dict

Heat supplied to the column through its wall in each step, J (negative when the column is cooled).

residual float

Normalized residual error of Subraveti, Karimi and Gazzani (2026, eq 2): over the steps, the largest 100 x sum of squares of the change of the dimensionless profiles at the end of the step from the previous cycle; filled in by Cycle.run.

profile_change float

Largest change of the column profiles over the cycle (dimensionless, see ColumnModel.profile_change); filled in by Cycle.run.

buffers holds the recorded streams (name to StreamRecord). Steps that read a record get it before they run, and outlets with a record_as name store their stream after they run, so a record made in one cycle is still available to steps earlier in the next cycle (for example the heavy reflux tank).

docs.title: run(model, initial_state, max_cycles=600, tolerance=0.5, consecutive=5, report_every=25, verbose=True, keep_cycles=10, criterion='both', profile_tolerance=0.001, accelerate=False, acceleration_memory=5, acceleration_start=None, acceleration_every=3, acceleration_stop=0.0001, residual_tolerance=1e-05, acceleration_max_jump=100.0)
docs.text:
Repeat the cycle until cyclic steady state.

Two tests of steady state are available, both checked over consecutive cycles in a row:

"mass_balance"  the key component mass balance error over a cycle
                is below ``tolerance`` (%), the usual criterion in
                the literature
"profiles"      no profile of the column changes by more than
                ``profile_tolerance`` over a cycle (dimensionless)
"both"          both of the above (default)
"residual"      the normalized residual error (eq 2 of Subraveti,
                Karimi and Gazzani 2026, ``CyclePerformance.residual``)
                is below ``residual_tolerance`` and the mass
                balance error below ``tolerance``, the criterion
                of that paper (use with ``consecutive=1``)

The mass balance alone can be met while the column is still slowly warming or loading, so "both" is the safer choice; use "mass_balance" to apply only the usual mass balance rule.

Acceleration (see swingpy.acceleration) starts some cycles from an extrapolated state instead of the end of the last cycle:

accelerate="graves_morris"   or another vector Steffensen method of
                             ``acceleration.STEFFENSEN_METHODS``
                             (Subraveti, Karimi and Gazzani 2026):
                             ``acceleration_start`` plain cycles
                             (3 by default), then an extrapolation
                             every ``acceleration_every`` cycles
                             until the residual is below

accelerate=True or "anderson"  Anderson mixing of the last

docs.title: swingpy.cycles
docs.text:
A family of single-column VSA cycles built from optional steps.

vsa_cycle assembles one cycle from the steps of the cycle synthesis of Haghpanah et al. (2013), AIChE J. 59, 4735, https://doi.org/10.1002/aic.14192 (their Figures 2 and 6):

FEED   adsorption at P_H; the raffinate is recorded
BLOW   co-current blowdown to P_I            (depressurization="blowdown")
EQDN   co-current pressure equalization       (depressurization="equalization")
HREF   heavy reflux at P_I, optional: a fraction of the extract enters
       the feed end at a constant molar flow while the product end is
       held at P_I; the refluxed gas is subtracted from the product
EVAC   counter-current evacuation to P_L; recorded as the extract
LREF   light reflux at P_L, optional: raffinate purges the column from
       the product end, the gas leaving the feed end is product
EQUP   receiving side of the equalization (depressurization="equalization")
LPPR   light product pressurization with the raffinate, then PRES with
       feed to P_H                            (pressurization="light product")
PRES   pressurization with feed               (pressurization="feed")

The seven cycles of the article are presets of this function in this module (HAGHPANAH_2013).

Pressure changes are either prescribed, as in the article (an exponential approach at rate over a given step time), or driven by vacuum pumps of given interstitial velocity, ended when the pressure is reached (give blowdown_velocity or evacuation_velocity). The equalization is always the single column treatment: the donor follows a prescribed pressure history and its outflow is recorded, the receiver takes that recorded flow in through its product end.

The function builds the cycle only; the column model (pressure drop law, mass transfer, heat transfer) is chosen independently when the cycle is run.

Basic four-step cycle of Figure 2, run in the order FEED, BLOW, EVAC, PRES.

The step ends when the closed feed end reaches 0.99 P_H, at most after t_ads; a feed pressurization step (PRES) then completes the pressurization. With pressure_limited_lpp=False the recorded flow is imposed whatever the pressure and the step ends at P_H, the unibed treatment of the article, which over-pressurizes the product end.

5-step cycle with one pressure equalization and feed pressurization, Figure 6d: FEED, EQDN, EVAC, EQUP, PRES.

The two columns of the equalization are coupled through a recorded stream: the donor blows down from P_H through its product end to the intermediate pressure of eq. 9 of the article, P_I = (P_H + P_L) / 2 - kappa with kappa = 0.041 bar, and the receiver takes in the recorded gas through its product end. docs.title: swingpy.streams
docs.text:
Recorded gas streams that couple one step of a cycle to another.

In a multi-bed plant the effluent of one column feeds another one at the same time: the raffinate of the adsorption step pressurizes a column (light product pressurization) or purges it (light reflux), and part of the extract is sent back to the feed end (heavy reflux). SwingPy simulates a single column, so such a stream is recorded while one step runs and played back when the receiving step runs (the single-bed or "unibed" approach). Records are replayed interval by interval, conserving the net recorded moles (gas that flowed back into the source column is not replayed).

Moles of each component available for replay in each sampling interval (components x intervals).

Gas can flow back into the source column through the recorded end, for example at the start of a feed step that begins below the outlet pressure. That gas comes out of the same stream, so it is subtracted from what left before or after it: the replayable moles follow the running maximum of the net moles that have left, never negative. A replay therefore never returns more than the net moles the source delivered, and returns exactly the recorded moles when no gas flowed back.

docs.title: swingpy.acceleration
docs.text:
Faster approach to cyclic steady state by vector acceleration of the cycle map.

Two families are available:

  • SteffensenAccelerator: the vector extensions of Steffensen's method compared for adsorption cycles by Subraveti, Karimi and Gazzani, Ind. Eng. Chem. Res. 65 (2026) 9656, https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.iecr.6c00407 (Table 1), with their schedule: plain cycles first, then an extrapolation every few cycles, and plain cycles only once the residual is small. Their best method overall is Graves-Morris.
  • AndersonAccelerator: Anderson mixing of the last few cycles.

Anderson acceleration:

One cycle maps the state of the column at its start to the state at its end, s -> F(s); cyclic steady state is the fixed point s = F(s). Repeating the cycle converges linearly, and slow modes (a column that keeps warming or loading a little each cycle) can take hundreds of cycles. Anderson acceleration combines the last few iterates to extrapolate towards the fixed point: with residuals g_k = F(s_k) - s_k it finds the weights that minimise the norm of their combination and moves to the same combination of the F(s_k).

Safeguards: the extrapolated state is projected back into the physical range (mole fractions between 0 and 1, positive pressures, loadings and temperatures), and whenever a step makes the residual grow markedly the history is dropped and a plain cycle follows. The performance indicators and the steady state tests are always those of a simulated cycle, never of an extrapolated state.

docs.title: SteffensenAccelerator
docs.text:
Vector Steffensen extrapolation of the cycle map (Subraveti, Karimi and Gazzani 2026).

The schedule is that of the paper: start plain cycles, an extrapolation at the next one, then an extrapolation after every every plain cycles; once the residual of a cycle falls below stop_residual no further extrapolation is made, so the last cycles to steady state are plain ones. Each extrapolation uses the last two plain cycles: D -> F(D) -> F(F(D)).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default model

The ColumnModel (for the layout of the state).

required method

A key of STEFFENSEN_METHODS ("graves_morris" by default, the best method of the paper).

'graves_morris' start

Plain cycles before the first extrapolation (3 in the paper).

3 every

Plain cycles between two extrapolations (3 in the paper, at least 2).

3 stop_residual

Residual (Cycle.residual) below which no more extrapolations are made (1e-4 in the paper).

0.0001 max_jump

Safeguard, not in the paper: an extrapolation that moves the state more than max_jump times the change over the last plain cycle (|new - F(D)| > max_jump |u|) is discarded and the plain cycle kept. The scalar parameter of every variant is a ratio of inner products whose denominator can pass through zero (for Zienkiewicz-Lohner v.w): on the zeolite 13X VSA case one extrapolation had lambda = -1980, a jump of 1900 |u|, and the next cycle could not be integrated. A slow mode with a contraction factor a needs a jump of about 1 / (1 - a), so the default 100 keeps modes down to a = 0.99.

100.0

docs.title: swingpy.isotherms
docs.text:
Multicomponent adsorption isotherms.

Every isotherm in this module returns its result through the "Henry slope" H_i = q_i* / c_i, in m3/kg. The loading follows as q_i* = H_i c_i, and the linear driving force model needs c_i / q_i* = 1 / H_i, which can then be computed without dividing by a loading that may be zero.

Available: DualSiteLangmuir (computed inside the compiled kernel when numba is installed), Sips, Toth, ExtendedLangmuir and IAST. To add a new isotherm, write a class with a slopes(c, T) method that returns H with the same shape as c, a loadings(c, T) method and a total_saturation property.

The equilibrium loading of component i is

q_i* = qsb_i b_i c_i / (1 + sum_k b_k c_k) + qsd_i d_i c_i / (1 + sum_k d_k c_k)

with b_i = b0_i exp(-dUb_i / RT) and d_i = d0_i exp(-dUd_i / RT). Concentrations are in mol/m3 and loadings in mol/kg. Each parameter is a sequence with one value per gas component, in the order of GasMixture.components. A single-site Langmuir isotherm is obtained with qsd and d0 equal to zero.

docs.title: Sips dataclass
docs.text:
Extended Sips (Langmuir-Freundlich) isotherm for mixtures.

q_i* = qs_i (b_i c_i)^n_i / (1 + sum_k (b_k c_k)^n_k)

with b_i = b0_i exp(-dU_i / RT), n_i(T) = n0_i + alpha_i (1 - T_ref / T) and qs_i(T) = qs0_i exp(chi_i (1 - T / T_ref)). With exponent_form="linear" the exponent is n_i(T) = n0_i + alpha_i (T / T_ref - 1), the form of Do (Adsorption Analysis, 1998); a capacity written exp(chi (T / T_ref - 1)) is this one with the sign of chi reversed. With n = 1 it is the competitive Langmuir isotherm. Concentrations in mol/m3, loadings in mol/kg, one value per gas component for every parameter.

For n < 1 the slope q*/c grows without bound as c goes to zero (the Freundlich limit). The slope is therefore evaluated at no less than minimum_concentration, so the linear driving force rate stays finite, while the loading itself still goes to zero with c.

docs.title: IAST
docs.text:
Ideal adsorbed solution theory: mixture equilibrium from pure-component isotherms.

For a gas of concentrations c_i, IAST finds the concentrations c_i0 of the pure components that have the same spreading pressure and whose adsorbed mole fractions x_i = c_i / c_i0 add up to one; then 1 / q_total = sum_i x_i / q_i0(c_i0) and q_i = x_i q_total. It needs only the pure-component isotherms and is the usual prediction of mixture adsorption when mixture data are lacking.

The equations are solved in every cell by a damped Newton method on ln c_i0. Spreading pressures use closed forms for single-component DualSiteLangmuir, ExtendedLangmuir and Sips isotherms and Gauss-Legendre quadrature for any other (for example Toth).

docs.title: MacroporeLDF dataclass
docs.text:
Linear driving force rate controlled by molecular diffusion in macropores.

The rate constant of component i is

k_i = (c_i / q_i*) 15 eps_p D_p / r_p^2,   with D_p = D_m / tortuosity,

where q_i* is expressed per cubic metre of adsorbent so that c_i / q_i* is dimensionless (q_i* in mol/kg times the particle density), the Glueckauf approximation for diffusion in a spherical particle.

A component that the solid barely holds (q_i* / c_i close to zero, for example nitrogen displaced by water) gets an enormous rate constant, which only means that it is at equilibrium; such rates are capped at max_rate (1/s), far above any rate that matters, so that the equations do not become needlessly stiff.

docs.title: SeriesLDF dataclass
docs.text:
Linear driving force for a bidisperse particle, with the film, macropore and micropore resistances added in series (Glueckauf; Ruthven, Principles of Adsorption and Adsorption Processes, 1984, Eq. 8.53 and 8.54):

1 / k_i = K_i / (a_p k_f) + K_i R_p^2 / (Omega_m eps_p D_p,i) + r_c^2 / (Omega_c D_c,i),
K_i = rho_p q_i* / c_i,   D_c,i / r_c^2 = (D_c0 / r_c^2)_i exp(-E_a,i / RT),

where K_i is the dimensionless slope of the isotherm per volume of particle (the secant q*/c, as in MacroporeLDF), a_p the external area per volume of particle (3 / R_p for spheres, 2 / R_p for cylinders) and Omega the LDF factors (15 for spheres, 8 for cylinders). This is a single LDF that stands in for a bi-LDF model, where the macropore gas and the micropore loading are separate states; it is exact for a linear isotherm at long times and an approximation otherwise, so say so when you use it.

docs.title: ParticleDiffusion dataclass
docs.text:
Fickian diffusion inside spherical particles (or crystals), resolved in concentric shells, instead of a linear driving force:

dq/dt = D / r^2 d/dr (r^2 dq/dr),   q(r_p) = q*(c, T) at the surface.

This is the model of uptake controlled by diffusion in the micropores of a crystal or a carbon molecular sieve, where it matters for kinetic separations; for a single particle at constant surface loading it reproduces the exact solution of Crank (The Mathematics of Diffusion, 1975, Eq. 6.20), to which a linear driving force with k = 15 D / r_p^2 is the Glueckauf approximation.

The particle is divided into shells shells, thinner towards the surface, and solved by finite volumes; the uptake of a cell is the flux through the particle surface, so mass is conserved exactly.

docs.title: swingpy.model
docs.text:
Finite volume model of a nonisothermal, nonisobaric adsorption column.

The column is described by a one-dimensional, axially dispersed plug flow model of an ideal gas mixture with any number of components, linear driving force uptake, a bed energy balance with heat of adsorption and heat loss to the wall, a wall energy balance, and Darcy or Ergun pressure drop. The equations are written in dimensionless, conservative form and solved on N equal cells.

Scaling. Pressure is divided by a reference pressure P0, temperature by T0, velocity by v0, length by the column length L, time by L / v0 and loadings by a reference loading q_s0. With L = 1 m and v0 = 1 m/s the dimensionless time equals time in seconds.

State vector. For n components the state holds, in this order:

y          n - 1 independent mole fractions, N values each
P          pressure, N values
x          n loadings, N values each
T          bed temperature, N values
T_wall     wall temperature, N values
bookkeeping  running integrals at both ends: n component fluxes,
             the enthalpy flux and the machine work, per end

The bookkeeping integrals make purity, recovery, energy and balance errors as accurate as the time integration itself.

docs.title: simulate(step, state, n_output=50, rtol=1e-05, atol=1e-07, max_evaluations=40000, fallback=True)
docs.text:
Integrate one step from its start to step.duration, or until its stop condition is met.

The bookkeeping integrals are reset at the start, so the returned flows and work belong to this step only. A step whose stop condition already holds is skipped and returns a zero-length result.

The stiff BDF solver is used first. The upwind side of each face follows the local velocity, so the right hand side is not smooth where the velocity changes sign; in a step whose gas is nearly at rest over part of the column (a blowdown or evacuation of a short, very permeable bed) Newton's method then keeps failing and BDF can take hundreds of thousands of evaluations. After max_evaluations right hand side evaluations the step is restarted with LSODA, which switches between non-stiff and stiff methods and handles this far better (a 2 s blowdown of a 1 cm bed: 81 000 evaluations with BDF, 11 500 with LSODA). max_evaluations=None keeps BDF however long it takes. With fallback=False the step raises StepTooStiff instead of switching to LSODA (used to discard an extrapolated cycle start that turns out to be hard to integrate).

docs.title: swingpy.plotting
docs.text:
Figures of SwingPy (they need matplotlib: pip install matplotlib).

Every figure follows one engineering journal style. The axes are open (no top or right spine), the ticks point outwards, there is no grid, the type is an Arial-metric sans serif, legends have no frame, panel letters stand on the title line, and each figure is saved twice: as a 300 dpi PNG and, next to it, as a vector PDF.

The figures carry no colour except in the position-time maps. Curves are told apart by their grey level and their line style. Results of the model are drawn as lines without markers; open markers (outline only, no fill) are kept for measured or published values, where there is no line to draw. Maps use the perceptually uniform viridis scale with labelled contours, as recommended by Crameri, Shephard and Heron, Nat. Commun. 11 (2020) 5444.

Cycle steps are named by four-letter codes (see STEP_CODES): PRES for pressurization with feed, FEED for the feed (adsorption) step, BLOW for blowdown, EVAC for evacuation, and so on. A figure writes the name a step was given; when a long name does not fit, its code is written instead.

docs.title: Steps and cycles
docs.text:
A step is two boundary conditions, one per column end, and a duration (or a stop condition). The same few classes cover every common step:

Step Feed end (Z = 0) Product end (Z = 1) Feed pressurization PressurizationInlet Closed Adsorption FeedInlet or FlowInlet PressureOutlet Blowdown (co-current) Closed PressureOutlet or VacuumPump Evacuation (counter-current) PressureOutlet or VacuumPump Closed Purge with a gas PressureOutlet FlowInlet Light product pressurization or light reflux Closed or PressureOutlet BufferInlet Heavy reflux TankInlet PressureOutlet Adsorption with a recycle into the feed MixingInlet PressureOutlet Any step through a valve Valve Valve Equalization, purge supply between beds Valve to a RecordedPressure (donor) BufferInlet (receiver)

docs.title: A family of VSA cycles
docs.text:
swingpy.cycles.vsa_cycle builds a single-column VSA cycle from optional steps, the building blocks of the cycle synthesis of Haghpanah et al., AIChE J. 59 (2013) 4735: adsorption (FEED), then blowdown (BLOW) or pressure equalization (EQDN), an optional heavy reflux at the intermediate pressure (HREF), evacuation (EVAC), an optional light reflux at the low pressure (LREF), the receiving side of the equalization (EQUP), and pressurization with light product (LPPR, completed by PRES) or with feed (PRES).

from swingpy.cycles import vsa_cycle

cycle = vsa_cycle({"CO2": 0.15, "N2": 0.85}, t_ads=60.0, feed_velocity=0.3, high=1.0, low=0.03,
                  intermediate=0.07, t_blow=60.0, t_evac=100.0, t_lr=5.0)          # five steps, LPP and LR
cycle = vsa_cycle({"CO2": 0.15, "N2": 0.85}, t_ads=80.0, feed_velocity=0.5, high=1.0, low=0.03,
                  intermediate=0.474, depressurization="equalization", t_eq=60.0,
                  t_hr=5.0, reflux_ratio=0.5, t_evac=130.0)                          # PE, HR and LPP

Pressure changes are prescribed (an exponential approach at rate over t_blow or t_evac) or driven by vacuum pumps of given interstitial velocity (blowdown_velocity, evacuation_velocity), the step then ending when P_I or P_L is reached. The heavy reflux feeds back reflux_ratio of the recorded extract at constant molar flow (TankInlet) and is subtracted from the product; the light reflux uses the first t_lr seconds of the recorded raffinate and the light product pressurization the rest. The seven configurations of the article are presets in the same module (HAGHPANAH_2013, by name: basic_four_step, four_step_lpp, five_step_lpp_lr, six_step_lpp_lr_hr, five_step_pe_fp, five_step_pe_lpp, six_step_pe_lpp_hr) with the feed and pressures of the article and every step time and pressure as an argument; the column model is chosen independently of the cycle (examples/setups/cycles.py pairs them with the model of the article and its operating points).

docs.title: Coupled steps
docs.text:
In a plant the effluent of one column feeds another one at the same time. SwingPy simulates one column, so an outlet records its stream (record_as="raffinate") and a later step replays it (BufferInlet("raffinate")); TankInlet replays a fraction of a recorded stream at its mean composition. A replayed stream can be limited to the pressure it was produced at (max_pressure). The replay is conservative: each sampling interval of the record delivers exactly the moles that left in it, so a sharp start (a pressure equalization opening onto an empty column) is replayed with the right amount. BufferInlet(..., composition={"N2": 1.0}) replays only the recorded molar flow, with another gas: the single column treatment of pressure equalization with pure product. PressurizationInlet and FlowInlet accept the name of a record as their composition (with default_composition for the first cycle) and then use its mean gas, for example pressurization or purge with the product of the feed step of another column. MixingInlet(molar_flow, composition, buffer="recycle") adds a recorded stream, spread evenly over the step, to a fresh feed at fixed molar flow: the outlet of an earlier step sent back with the feed. The fresh moles count as the feed stream and the recycled ones as recycle, so recovery refers to the fresh feed only; label the outlet that fills the tank stream="recycle" and the two cancel in the cycle balance.

A feed inlet can also take its gas from a recorded stream, FeedInlet(0.2, "light", default_composition={"N2": 1.0}): the mean composition of the record, as from a well mixed tank (light product pressurization at a constant velocity).

docs.title: Stop conditions
docs.text: stop=PressureReached(0.1, location="feed", rising=False) ends a step when the pressure at one end crosses a value; the duration is then the longest the step may last. With vacuum pumps of fixed capacity, the time to reach a vacuum is a result of the simulation.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text: Every outlet and inlet carries a stream label. Cycle(key_component="CO2") computes the purity and recovery of the stream labelled product, the specific energy from the compressor and pump work of every step, and the productivity; CyclePerformance.streams gives the moles of every component in every stream.

docs.title: Pure-component gas properties
docs.text:
swingpy.data holds pure-component properties of common gases (CO2, N2, O2, Ar, CH4, CO, He): molar mass, ideal-gas heat capacity and viscosity at 298.15 K, and Fuller diffusion volume. data.gas_sources() names the source of each kind of property. Your own components are added with data.register_gas.

from swingpy import data

data.list_gases()
data.gas_properties("CO2")

docs.title: Adsorbents
docs.text:
SwingPy does not ship adsorbents: the isotherm, heats of adsorption and particle properties of a material come from you, in Python or in a specification file (see Problem specifications).

from swingpy import Adsorbent, DualSiteLangmuir, MacroporeLDF

sorbent = Adsorbent(
    name="my zeolite",
    isotherm=DualSiteLangmuir(qsb=(3.09, 5.84), qsd=(2.54, 0.0), b0=(8.65e-7, 2.5e-6), d0=(2.63e-8, 0.0),
                              dUb=(-36641.0, -15800.0), dUd=(-35691.0, 0.0)),
    heat_of_adsorption=(36641.0, 15800.0), density=1130.0, particle_radius=1e-3, particle_voidage=0.35,
    tortuosity=3.0, heat_capacity=1070.0, adsorbed_phase_heat_capacity=30.7, kinetics=MacroporeLDF())

The examples use adsorbents reported in the literature, each with its sources: examples/setups/adsorbents.json, read by examples/setups/adsorbents.py (import setups; setups.adsorbent("zeolite-13x") from the examples folder).

docs.title: Gas mixtures
docs.text:
gas = data.gas(["CO2", "N2"], {"CO2": 0.15, "N2": 0.85}, temperature=298.15, pressure=1.0)

The heat capacity is the mole-fraction average, the viscosity follows Wilke's mixing rule and the molecular diffusivity the method of Fuller, Schettler and Giddings for the first two components. They are constants of the model: evaluate them at the feed conditions. data.gas_properties("CO2") returns the stored properties of a pure gas.

docs.title: Your own gases
docs.text: data.register_gas("C2H6", molar_mass=30.07e-3, heat_capacity=52.5, viscosity=0.93e-5, diffusion_volume=44.88)

docs.title: Valves, layers, dead volume and IAST
Valves
docs.text:
Valve(cv, pressure) connects a column end to a reservoir with a linear valve, molar flow = cv × (upstream − downstream pressure), cv in mol/(s bar). The face pressure and the flow are solved together with the pressure drop over half a cell.

Valve(0.035, 1.013, stream="waste")                                     # blowdown to the waste line
Valve(1.0, 3.0, direction="in", composition={"N2": 1.0}, stream="feed")   # filling from a 3 bar header
Valve(56.0, 14.997, extra_outflow=0.008, stream="product")               # product valve and a fixed side draw

The reservoir pressure can be a number, a function of time, or a RecordedPressure: the face pressure that another step recorded (record_as) in the previous cycle. This is how a bed equalizes with, or supplies purge to, another bed in a single-column simulation: the donor vents through its valve into the pressure history of the receiving step, the receiving step replays the donor's gas (BufferInlet), and at cyclic steady state the two are consistent.

A gas supplied from a line (a recorded product, a header) can be limited to the pressure of that line: FlowInlet(..., max_pressure=15.0), BufferInlet(..., max_pressure=...).

docs.title: Dead volume
docs.text: Column(dead_volume_feed=..., dead_volume_product=...) adds well-mixed gas volumes (m3) at the ends of the bed: pipes, distributors, valve bodies. They hold gas but no adsorbent and slow the pressure and composition changes at that end; the mass and energy inventories include them.

docs.title: Layered beds
docs.text:
from swingpy import LayeredBed
bed = LayeredBed([(carbon, 0.3), (zeolite, 0.7)])        # two Adsorbent objects of your own
model = ColumnModel(column, bed, gas)

Layers are listed from the feed end, as (adsorbent, length fraction) or (adsorbent, length fraction, bed voidage). Every layer keeps its own isotherm, kinetics, density, heat capacity, heats of adsorption, particle size and voidage. The balances use the superficial flux through every face and the voidage of every cell, and the permeability, inertial term and dispersion of every face follow from the particle size and voidage on both sides of it, so gas and heat are conserved exactly across layer boundaries.

Layered beds, IAST, Sips, Toth and any kinetics model run with the compiled (numba) backend: the isotherm slopes and rate constants are evaluated in Python and passed to the compiled transport and energy equations.

docs.title: Mixture equilibrium by IAST
docs.text: IAST([pure_1, pure_2, ...]) predicts mixture adsorption from single-component isotherms (any of DualSiteLangmuir, ExtendedLangmuir, Sips, Toth with one component), by solving the ideal adsorbed solution theory in every cell. For equal saturation capacities it reduces to the extended Langmuir isotherm, which SwingPy reproduces to machine precision.

docs.title: Extended Langmuir and pressure-dependent kinetics
docs.text: ExtendedLangmuir(henry, affinity, dU) has separate capacity and affinity constants, so a component can adsorb in proportion to its concentration without taking up sites (affinity zero), as a weakly adsorbed gas in its linear range. PressureScaledLDF(rates, reference_pressure) gives rate constants inversely proportional to pressure, the behaviour of macropore molecular diffusion.

docs.title: Resistances in series
docs.text: SeriesLDF(micropore_rates, activation_energies, macropore_diffusivities, film_coefficient, micropore_factor, macropore_factor, area_factor) is one LDF rate with the film, macropore and micropore resistances added in series (Glueckauf; Ruthven 1984): 1/k_i = K_i/(a_p k_f) + K_i R_p2/(Ω_m ε_p D_p,i) + r_c2/(Ω_c D_c,i), with K_i = ρ_p q_i*/c_i and D_c/r_c2 = (D_c0/r_c2) exp(−E_a/RT). It stands in for the bi-LDF model of the same papers, which keeps the macropore gas and the micropore loading as separate states; that model is not in SwingPy. The series form is exact for a linear isotherm at long times and an approximation otherwise.

docs.title: Heat through the wall
docs.text:
ColumnModel.wall_heat(result) gives the heat that crossed the wall in a step, from the outer heat transfer coefficient and the wall temperatures over time; CyclePerformance.heat_by_step lists it per step. An insulated column (Column(outer_heat_transfer=0.0)) exchanges none.

Order of the components

The model solves for every mole fraction but the last, which is one minus the others. Put the most abundant carrier gas last (N2 in flue gas). A trace component with a sharp front must not be last: it would absorb the small errors of all the others and the integration would slow down badly.

Rate constants of the macropore LDF model are capped at MacroporeLDF(max_rate=1000) 1/s: a component that the solid barely holds would otherwise get an enormous rate constant, which only means it is at equilibrium.

docs.title: Ideal gas
docs.text: The column model treats the gas as ideal, as is usual for pressure and vacuum swing processes near atmospheric pressure: for flue gas near 1 bar the compressibility factor is 0.999, an error of 0.05 to 0.15 % in the gas density, well within the other uncertainties of a model. At high pressure with much CO2 the ideal gas underestimates the density by several per cent; real gas behaviour is one of the possible extensions of SwingPy.

docs.title: Outputs and figures
docs.text:
Every simulation can be reported in one call: the numbers as CSV files, the standard figures of adsorption processes as PNG and PDF (with matplotlib, pip install matplotlib), and Summary.md, a readable summary.

from swingpy.report import report_breakthrough, report_run

report_breakthrough(model, result, "Output/Breakthrough")    # a single feed step
report_run(model, run, "Output/Cycle")                       # a cycle run (Cycle.run)

problem.report(run, "Output/Cycle")                          # the same for a specification (swingpy.spec)

The figures below come from tools/Make gallery.py: a breakthrough and a four-step VSA cycle on zeolite 13X (examples/specs/VSA zeolite 13X flue gas.yaml).

docs.title: Numbers (swingpy.analysis, no matplotlib needed)
docs.text:
Function Content breakthrough_metrics(model, result, component) times at which the outlet reaches 5, 50 and 95 % of the feed mole fraction, stoichiometric time, amount retained (exact), dynamic capacity, mass transfer zone, peak outlet temperature step_table(model, results) per step: duration, pressures at both ends, moles of each component through each end, stream labels, machine work, heat through the wall cycle_summary(model, run) purity, recovery, specific energy, productivity, cycle time, balance error, profile change, composition of every stream stream_table, convergence_table, profile_table, cycle_history_table streams per cycle; KPIs of every cycle; profiles at the end of every step; time series of one cycle at chosen positions and at both ends end_flows(model, result, end), column_profiles(model, state) flows and composition crossing an end; profiles of one state export_run(model, run, folder), export_breakthrough(model, result, folder) all of the above as CSV files

Flows are in mol/s and positive out of the column, pressures in bar, temperatures in K, loadings in mol/kg.

docs.title: Figures (swingpy.plotting)
docs.text:
All figures share one journal style (apply_style()): open axes, outward ticks, no grid, Arial-metric sans serif type, frameless legends, titles in regular weight with the panel letter on the same line, PNG at 300 dpi plus a vector PDF.

  • Curves computed by the model are lines only, told apart by grey level (black, #555555, #8C8C8C, #B8B8B8) and line style (series_style(i)); a lone curve is solid black (single_style()).
  • Measured or published values are the only points: open markers with no fill (open_marker_style(i)), so model and data can never be mistaken for each other.
  • Time histories separate the steps with dotted lines and the cycles with dashed ones, name the steps above the axes, and carry no shading.
  • Quantities per step or per kind of energy are lollipops: a thin stem from zero to an open marker, one row per step.
  • Position-time maps use the viridis scale (Crameri, Shephard and Heron, Nat. Commun. 11 (2020) 5444: perceptually uniform, readable in grey) with white contours at 10, 50 and 90 % of the range and always a colour bar.

docs.text:
The four-step cycle of the same example, run with plain cycles from a column filled with nitrogen at 0.1 bar: cyclic steady state (mass balance error below 0.5 % and profile change below 10−3 for five cycles in a row) after 360 cycles, purity 79.39 %, recovery 36.64 %.

docs.title: The column model
docs.text: SwingPy describes a packed column as a one-dimensional, axially dispersed plug flow of an ideal gas mixture through a bed of porous particles.

docs.title: Balances
docs.text:
For component \(i\) in the gas, with interstitial velocity \(v\), total concentration \(C = P/RT\) and bed voidage \(\varepsilon\):

\[ \frac{\partial (y_i C)}{\partial t} + \frac{\partial (v\, y_i C)}{\partial z} = \frac{\partial}{\partial z}\left(D_L C \frac{\partial y_i}{\partial z}\right) - \frac{1-\varepsilon}{\varepsilon}\,\frac{\partial q_i}{\partial t} \]

with \(q_i\) the loading per volume of particles. Uptake follows the linear driving force model,

\[ \frac{\partial q_i}{\partial t} = k_i \left(q_i^* - q_i\right), \]

where the equilibrium loading \(q_i^*\) comes from the isotherm and \(k_i\) is either constant or obtained from macropore diffusion, \(k_i = 15\,\varepsilon_p D_{m}/(\tau r_p^2)\, c_i/q_i^*\).

For uptake controlled by diffusion inside the particles (crystals or carbon molecular sieves, kinetic separations), ParticleDiffusion(rates, shells=12) resolves Fick's law in every particle on shells that thin towards the surface, with the surface at equilibrium with the gas; rates are the diffusional time constants D/r2 (1/s).

The bed energy balance includes the heat capacities of the gas, the solid and the adsorbed phase, axial conduction, the heat of adsorption and heat transfer to the wall; the wall has its own energy balance with heat loss to the surroundings. The velocity follows from the local pressure gradient through Darcy's law or the Ergun equation.

docs.title: Boundary conditions
docs.text: At an inlet, Danckwerts conditions set composition and temperature; at an outlet, gradients vanish. The flow at each end is set either by a velocity or molar flow (feed, purge, vacuum pump) or by a pressure (pressurization, blowdown, a back-pressure regulator), the other quantity following from the pressure drop over half a cell.

docs.title: Numerical method
docs.text:
The equations are written in dimensionless, conservative form and discretized on equal finite volumes. Face values on the upwind side are reconstructed with first-order upwind, van Leer, Superbee or WENO, choosing the upwind side face by face from the local velocity, so that flow reversal inside the column is handled. The resulting system is integrated by a variable-order BDF method with a sparse Jacobian. Running integrals of the component and enthalpy fluxes and of the machine work at both ends make purity, recovery, energy and balance errors as accurate as the integration itself.

The upwind side of each face follows the local velocity, so the equations are not smooth where the gas comes to rest. In a step where it is nearly at rest over part of the column (the blowdown of a short, very permeable bed) Newton's method in BDF then keeps failing; after 40 000 evaluations of the right hand side (simulate(..., max_evaluations=...)) the step is restarted with LSODA, which agrees with BDF to 10−8 in the state and is far faster there.

docs.title: Cyclic steady state
docs.text: Cycle.run repeats the cycle until steady state: by default the key component mass balance must close within a tolerance and the column profiles must stop changing, both over five cycles in a row. Either test alone can be met while the other is not, depending on the cycle.

docs.title: Faster approach to steady state
docs.text:
Cycle.run(..., accelerate=True) starts each cycle from an Anderson extrapolation of the last few cycles instead of the end of the last one. It works best when the approach to steady state is gradual: steady state is then reached in fewer cycles, with the same purity and recovery. When the slow part of the approach is a front travelling through the column (for example a bed that warms from one end over many cycles), extrapolation cannot predict it; the method then falls back to plain cycles and takes as many as without it. The results are always those of simulated cycles, so acceleration changes how fast steady state is reached, never where it is.

Cycle.run(..., accelerate="graves_morris") uses instead the vector extensions of Steffensen's method compared for adsorption cycles by Subraveti, Karimi and Gazzani (Ind. Eng. Chem. Res. 65 (2026) 9656, Table 1): lemarechal, sedogbo, a1, a4, irons_tuck, b1, zienkiewicz_lohner, graves_morris, c1, c2, macleod_m6 and epsilon2. Each extrapolation uses two successive plain cycles D → F(D) → F(F(D)); with u = F(D) − D, v = F(F(D)) − F(D) and w = v − u, Graves-Morris starts the next cycle from F(D) − (uᵀv / uᵀw) v. The schedule is that of the paper: three plain cycles, then an extrapolation every acceleration_every (3) cycles, and none once the residual is below acceleration_stop (10−4). The residual of the paper (its eq 2: over the steps, the largest 100 × sum of squares of the change of the dimensionless profiles from the previous cycle) is recorded in CyclePerformance.residual, and criterion="residual" applies the steady state test of the paper (residual below residual_tolerance, 10−5, and mass balance error below 0.5 %). A cycle that starts from an extrapolated state is run without the LSODA fallback: if one of its steps needs more than 40 000 evaluations it raises StepTooStiff, the extrapolation is discarded (counted in the accelerator's rejected) and the cycle is run again from the simulated state. On adiabatic pilot-scale columns some extrapolated states were otherwise integrated for more than 40 minutes. The conference paper that preceded the 2026 article (Subraveti et al., FOCAPD 2024) prints the Graves-Morris step as F(D) − (wᵀw / uᵀw) v; for a scalar linear sequence that form does not give the limit, while the 2026 form, used here, gives it exactly (Aitken's Δ2).

docs.title: Trace components
docs.text: The model solves the mole fractions of all components but the last; the last is 1 minus the others. Components present at ppm levels (CO2 traces, impurities) are nevertheless accurate in either position. For 1 ppm of CO2 in N2 fed to zeolite 13X for 2000 s, the CO2 profile computed with the default solver tolerances differs from a reference solution (absolute tolerance 10−12) by 0.3 % of the feed mole fraction when CO2 is solved directly and by 0.1 % when it is the last component, and the CO2 balance closes within 0.01 % and 0.03 %. At 420 ppm the two orders differ by 0.13 % at most. The order of the components is therefore free; a test keeps this so (tests/test_spec.py).

docs.title: Problem specifications
docs.text:
A whole problem can be written as a YAML or JSON file (or a Python dict): components, gas, adsorbent, bed, model options, streams, initial state and cycle. load_problem checks it, reports every error at once with its path, and builds the model and the cycle.

from swingpy.spec import load_problem

problem = load_problem("examples/specs/VSA zeolite 13X flue gas.yaml")
run = problem.run(max_cycles=300)
print(run.performance.purity, run.performance.recovery)

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
• Every physical quantity comes from the specification. Nothing about the gas, the adsorbent, the bed, the machines or the feed has a hidden default; a missing value is an error.
  • Units are explicit. A value is "<number> <unit>" ("1.2 m", "25 C", "36.6 kJ/mol") or a plain number in the base unit of its kind (swingpy.spec.BASE_UNITS). A unit of the wrong kind is an error.
  • Only numerical options have defaults: model.cells (30), model.scheme (weno), model.backend (auto), model.axial_dispersion (correlation), bed.include_pore_gas (false), bed.dead_volume (none), kinetics.max_rate (1000 1/s) and kinetics.shells (12).

docs.title: Layout
docs.text: Section Contents components Names, two or more. Any names: the data bank is not consulted. gas equation_of_state (ideal), molar_masses per component, heat_capacity, viscosity, molecular_diffusivity, adiabatic_constant. adsorbent particle_density, particle_radius, particle_voidage, tortuosity, heat_capacity, adsorbed_phase_heat_capacity, heat_of_adsorption per component, isotherm, kinetics. bed length, inner_radius, outer_radius, voidage, pressure_drop (darcy, ergun), axial_thermal_conductivity, wall (density, heat capacity, thermal conductivity), heat_transfer (inner, outer, ambient temperature), optional dead_volume and include_pore_gas. model reference (pressure, temperature, velocity used to scale the equations), numerical options. streams Named gas streams: composition per component (adding up to 1) and temperature. initial pressure, temperature, composition of the column at the start. cycle key_component, optional machines (efficiency, supply and discharge pressures every machine inherits unless it gives its own), steps.

docs.title: Isotherms
docs.text: model is one of langmuir, dual_site_langmuir, sips, toth, or python (with object: "module:function" for an isotherm object of your own), followed by one block of parameters per component. For sips and toth the unit of b0 sets the basis: m3/mol for concentrations, 1/bar (or 1/Pa, 1/kPa) for partial pressures; it must be the same for every component. The temperature dependence of the Sips exponent is n0 + alpha (1 − T_ref/T) by default; exponent_form: linear (at the level of model) selects n0 + alpha (T/T_ref − 1), the form of Do used by Hefti et al. (2015). For virial, give specific_area (m2/kg or m2/g) at the level of model, and per component K_inf (mol/(kg bar), as the papers give it), dH (negative), A0 (m2/mol), A1 (m2 K/mol), B0 (m4/mol2) and B1 (m4 K/mol2).

docs.title: Kinetics
docs.text: macropore_ldf (rate from the particle properties), constant_ldf and pressure_scaled_ldf (with rates per component), particle_diffusion (with rates D/r2 per component and shells), or series_ldf (with micropore_rates D_c0/r_c2, activation_energies and macropore_diffusivities per component, and film_coefficient, micropore_factor, macropore_factor, area_factor; see SeriesLDF).

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
Each step has a name, and either a duration or until (pressure, at: feed, product or mean, direction: rising or falling) with max_duration. Each end (feed_end, product_end, closed if omitted) is one of:

type Parameters closed feed stream, velocity, supply_pressure, efficiency pressure_inlet stream, pressure (a value or {ramp: exponential, from, to, rate}), supply_pressure, efficiency, optional record (the mean gas of a recorded stream; stream is used until it exists) outlet pressure (value or ramp), label, discharge_pressure, efficiency, optional record_as, check_valve vacuum_pump volumetric_flow or velocity, label, discharge_pressure, efficiency (a number or falling_vacuum), optional record_as replay record (a stream recorded with record_as), label, optional offset, max_pressure, stream (replay the recorded flow with this gas instead) tank record, fraction, temperature, label, supply_pressure, efficiency mixing_inlet stream (the fresh gas), molar_flow, record (the recycled stream), optional fraction, label (fresh, feed by default), recycle_label (recycle by default), supply_pressure, efficiency

label names the stream for the performance indicators (product, raffinate, ...); cycle.product_stream (default product) is the one purity and recovery refer to.

docs.title: Saving a problem built in Python
docs.text:
to_spec(model, cycle, initial) returns the specification of a problem built in Python, and save_problem(path, model, cycle, initial, header=...) writes it as YAML; load_problem builds an identical model and cycle from it. What a specification cannot express yet (layered beds, valves, functions of your own) is named in the error. The files in examples/specs were written this way from the cases they describe, and each is checked to give the same model, step by step.

from swingpy.spec import save_problem
save_problem("My case.yaml", model, cycle, dict(pressure=0.1, temperature=298.15, composition={"N2": 1.0}))

Further boundary types: flow_inlet (a fixed molar_flow, in mol/s, kmol/h or SLPM, from a stream or from a record with a stream used until the record exists; optional max_pressure). discharge_pressure: none or supply_pressure: none marks a stream without a machine (no work counted). For Toth isotherms, competitive: false treats the components independently; gas.adiabatic_constant: linear_co2 uses gamma = 1.395 - 0.105 y_CO2.
